title: 1 Cent - Elizabeth II (2nd portrait)

obverse.description: Bust of Queen Elizabeth II, as at 37 years of age, wearing tiara, facing right.
obverse.lettering_translation: Elizabeth II Queen by the grace of God

reverse.description: A maple twig is surrounded with the face value and the inscription "CANADA"

comments:
“In 1964, the British government decided to introduce a more mature portrait of Queen Elizabeth for national and Commonwealth coins. The new portrait design, by Arnold Machin, featured the Queen wearing a diadem instead of a laurel wreath. A copy of the design was sent to Canada and incorporated into the obverse for 1965.” - Standard Charlton Catalogue Volume I

1965 obverse varieties. “In 1965, difficulties were encountered in minting the cents, resulting in the introduction of a second variety. The first variety has small pearls at the edge and a flat field; the second variety has large pearls at the edge and a field that rises towards the edge. Another way of distinguishing the two obverses is the position of the “A” in “REGINA” in relation to the edge pearls: on small pearls, it points between two pearls, while on large pearls, it points towards one pearl.” - Standard Charlton catalog Volume I

1965 reverse varieties. “In addition, two reverses differing in style from 5 in the date were used in 1965. Obverse and reverse were used in all possible combinations, creating four varieties for the year.” - Standard Charlton catalog Volume I

“In 1977, the Mint struck test tokens with a considerably reduced weight and a diameter of 16 mm. The change was prompted by the rising price of copper, which had caused a loss on the production of the 1-cent coin. Unfortunately, the diameter of the token was the same as that used by the Toronto Transit Commission. The conflict resulted in the cancellation of the reduced-diameter cent.” - Standard Charlton Catalogue Volume I

1978 Composition: 98% copper, 1.75% tin, 0.25% zinc. Thickness (mm): 1.52
